failures.claim: The tests decide whether NEW BEST is visible only from `hidden`/`aria-hidden`. They never check the `is-out`/`is-back` classes that actually make the chip visible through CSS. If aria-hidden stopped matching the CSS state, the tests would still pass.
failures.evidence: visibleNewBest() walks ancestors checking only `e.hidden || e.getAttribute('aria-hidden') === 'true'`. In hud.ts, CSS visibility comes from `.ui-hud-new-best.is-out/.is-back`, and aria-hidden is set separately in newBest().

failures.claim: Under prefers-reduced-motion, the 'back' phase hides the chip with CSS visibility, but hud.ts still sets aria-hidden=false for that phase. For about 200 ms, screen readers treat the chip as present while it is visually gone. Small mismatch.
failures.evidence: hud.css: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ui-hud-new-best.is-back { visibility: hidden; } }`. hud.ts: `newBestChip.setAttribute('aria-hidden', String(phase === null))`.

blind.summary: B07 adds best-lap persistence. src/ui/best-laps.ts holds bestLapKey, a localStorage store with every access in try/catch, and an in-memory store for stages. race-ui reads the stored best on reset and writes on a new best, computing the NEW BEST show and hide ticks from tokens. The HUD gains one mustard chip under BEST that moves only by transform, has square top corners and no top border, and cuts under reduced motion. The results chip now reads NEW BEST LAP after a race that set a stored best. game.ts passes trackId, and a new stage file covers the HUD and results states. All gates pass (621 tests). Screenshots at 844x390 and 1440x900 show the NEW BEST tab tucked under the BEST chip in matching style, with TIME unmoved, and the results chip reading NEW BEST LAP as in the S5 mockup. Real race frames show the stored best and no stray chip. Tests drive the real game through its public play/step API, write the literal localStorage key, and cover every AC, including both ways storage can be blocked. Only nits remain: the visibility test checks aria-hidden rather than the CSS classes, and under reduced motion aria-hidden and the CSS disagree for about 200 ms. The diff matches the expected files (results.css was not needed), and it neither repeats existing work nor sniffs the environment.
